schemes.name: butterfly_field_wide_lanes
schemes.secondary_language: five three-storey pavilions under butterfly roofs, spread wider so no two plans touch and every gap is a lane
schemes.formal_principle: The field of V roofs is kept and the lanes are made real: spread 1.8 opens every gap to a lane a person walks down, so the pavilions read as a village with streets, not a cluster with cracks.
schemes.dominant_gesture: a field of V roofs with real lanes
schemes.reference_basis: development of field_under_butterfly_wings: the field of V roofs is kept; the jury's overlap, frontage and core remarks are answered
schemes.design_argument_ko: 겹치던 평면을 벌려 틈을 골목으로 만든다.

ops.why: Spread 1.8 answers the overlapping plans the jury saw: every pavilion stands clear and every gap is a lane.
Every roof still folds inward as a butterfly - the valley is the idea and is kept in every child.

schemes.name: butterfly_field_with_a_canopy
schemes.secondary_language: five pavilions under butterfly roofs, a shared canopy reaching toward the open side as the field's front
schemes.formal_principle: A field needs a front: the pavilions keep their valleys, and one canopy reaches toward the open side so the street reads an entry and the cluster gains the frontage hierarchy the jury missed.
schemes.dominant_gesture: a field of V roofs with a front canopy
schemes.reference_basis: development of field_under_butterfly_wings: the field of V roofs is kept; the jury's overlap, frontage and core remarks are answered
schemes.design_argument_ko: 열린 변으로 뻗는 캐노피가 밭에 정면과 입구를 준다.

ops.why: Five pavilions at the parent's scale and spacing.
Every roof still folds inward as a butterfly - the valley is the idea and is kept in every child.
A canopy toward the open side gives the field a front and an entry the jury said it lacked.

schemes.name: butterfly_field_toward_the_street
schemes.secondary_language: five pavilions under butterfly roofs, the whole field pushed toward the open side so it fronts the street
schemes.formal_principle: A field needs a front: the pavilions keep their valleys and the cluster moves toward the open side, so the street meets the first pavilions instead of a leftover strip and the empty west tip is filled.
schemes.reference_basis: development of field_under_butterfly_wings: the field of V roofs is kept; the jury's overlap, frontage and core remarks are answered
schemes.design_argument_ko: 밭 전체를 열린 변으로 밀어 거리가 첫 파빌리온과 만나게 한다.

ops.why: Five pavilions at the parent's scale and spacing.
Every roof still folds inward as a butterfly - the valley is the idea and is kept in every child.
The field grows toward the open side so its front reaches the street; the west tip stops being empty.

schemes.name: butterfly_field_of_four
schemes.secondary_language: four larger pavilions under shallower butterfly roofs, each plate big enough for its own core
schemes.formal_principle: Fewer, larger houses: four pavilions give each a floor plate that takes a core and a stair, and shallower valleys stop the pitch cutting the top floor - the field stays a field with fewer, stronger pieces.
schemes.reference_basis: development of field_under_butterfly_wings: the field of V roofs is kept; the jury's overlap, frontage and core remarks are answered
schemes.design_argument_ko: 네 채로 줄여 코어를 넣고 골을 얕게 해 최상층을 지킨다.

ops.why: Four pavilions answer the core-per-house remark: each plate is large enough for its own core.
Shallower valleys so the top floor is not cut by the pitch, as the jury noted.
